changelog.en: Add-on Store 2.0: the whole store now follows the new Tungsten brand. The setup shows a light banner with the new Tungsten Automation logo, and the list of available updates shows the Power PDF symbol for a Power PDF update. Nothing changes in how you use it.

Das Setup zeigt einen hellen Kopfbereich mit dem neuen Logo von Tungsten Automation, und die Liste der verfügbaren Updates zeigt bei einem Power-PDF-Update das Power-PDF-Symbol. An der Bedienung ändert sich nichts.

changelog.ar: Add-on Store 2.0: يتبع المتجر بأكمله الآن الهوية الجديدة لـ Tungsten. يعرض برنامج الإعداد شريطًا علويًا فاتحًا مع شعار Tungsten Automation الجديد، وتعرض قائمة التحديثات المتاحة رمز Power PDF عند وجود تحديث لـ Power PDF. لا يتغير شيء في طريقة الاستخدام.

complianceAudit.method: Checked all #include directives and linker inputs of PluginStore.vcxproj (Windows SDK incl. BCrypt/Crypt32 for SHA-256 and the ECDSA signature check, MFC/ATL, Tungsten Power PDF Plugin SDK only), the bundled UILayout and icon files (own work, icons drawn by client/res/make_icons.py) and the package contents. One third-party component: the Microsoft WebView2 SDK static loader (BSD-3-Clause), linked into PluginStore.zxt; its NOTICE lists only BSD-licensed .NET tooling that is not used. The bundled MSI is built with the WiX Toolset 3.14 (build tool only): since 1.9.13 it contains no WiX runtime parts (own dialogs, texts and banner; the quote page opens through explorer.exe; Windows Installer's Restart Manager closes Power PDF on request), checked in the Binary, CustomAction and Dialog tables of all 21 language versions. No credentials, personal data or third-party trademarks in the package. The only network service is the configured Add-on Store server (HTTPS). Since 1.9.8 the setup shows, on a Power PDF licensed with a serial number, a dialog whose button "Request a quote" opens Tungsten Automation's public quote page in the default browser (only on that click, never in silent installs); the setup itself sends nothing. The MSI also installs AddonStoreLink.exe (own code, no network access), which handles addonstore:// links by passing a validated package id to the client. Since 1.9.11 the store window page uses the Tungsten Plug-in UI kit, since 1.9.18 version 1.1.0 (client/third_party/tpui: own code of Tungsten Automation, MIT; CSS inlined into the page at build time, no network access). Since 1.9.18 the page also carries, as data embedded at build time, the brand font Red Hat Display 1.023 (Light, Regular, Medium, Bold; SIL Open Font License 1.1, which allows embedding and redistribution; declared in thirdParty, licence text in LICENSES.md) and the Tungsten Automation logo 2026 (original SVG of the Brand Book November 2026, property of Tungsten Automation, used per the Brand Book). Since 2.0.0 the setup banner shows the Tungsten Automation logo 2026 (original PNG of the brand package, only scaled) and the store window shows the Power PDF symbol of the original Tungsten Power PDF lockup (SVG, only the viewBox changed), both property of Tungsten Automation, used per the Brand Book.

externalServices.name: Add-on Store server (configurable; default addon.power-pdf.de, Azure address ppdf-store.azurewebsites.net)
externalServices.data: Catalog, search and package downloads; sends the Power PDF UI language, the beta channel flag and, only when the user or IT entered one, the customer code of a delivery (X-Customer-Code header). The catalog is also read once in the background about 15 seconds after Power PDF starts and after the store window closes, to show the update badge (IT can switch this off with the policy UpdateBadge = 0). No personal data, no documents.

externalServices.name: Tungsten Automation quote page (setup only, serial-number Power PDF)
externalServices.data: None from the setup: the button opens the public page in the default browser (tungstenautomation.de for German, .fr for French, .com otherwise); the browser then talks to that website as with any link.

elevation.reason: Installing, updating and removing add-ons writes to Power PDF's Plug-Ins folder in Program Files: one PowerShell step runs elevated after the UAC prompt, only when the user installs, updates or removes an add-on (the self-update starts msiexec the same way).
